(p-54) His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Nay!﴾ is a rebuke and a deterrence, meaning: the matter is not as they are upon, so let them desist. Here, according to many scholars, the speech is complete. Abu Hatim used to say: "Kallaa" is a beginning that connects with what follows, in the sense of "truly." ﴿Indeed, the record of the wicked﴾. Muqatil said: indeed the record of their deeds ﴿is in Sijjin﴾. Concerning Sijjin there are four opinions.

The first: it is the seventh earth. This is the view of Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, Ibn Zayd and Muqatil. It is narrated from Mujahid that he said: "Sijjin" is a rock beneath the seventh earth, and the record of the wicked is placed beneath it. This is a sign of their loss and an indication of the lowliness of their station.

The second: the meaning is that their record is in a low state (safal), as said by al-Hasan.

The third: it is ﴿in loss﴾, as said by Ikrimah.

The fourth: it is ﴿in confinement﴾, a form (fi‘}il) derived from "prison (sijn)," as said by Abu ‘Ubaydah.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And what will make you know what Sijjin is?﴾ This is an exaltation of its matter. Al-Zajjaj said: meaning, this is not something you or your people knew.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿It is a written record﴾, meaning: that book which is in Sijjin is a written record (p-55), i.e., inscribed. Ibn Qutaybah said: "al-raqm" means writing. Abu Dhu'ayb said:

"I recognized the abodes like the inscription of an ink-pot, which the Himyarite scribe writes out."

The fourth: the last of its taste is musk, [said by] Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, al-Farra’, Abu ‘Ubaydah, Ibn Qutaybah, al-Zajjaj and others.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And for that let the competitors compete﴾, meaning: let them strive to obtain it, and let them be eager for it through obedience to Allah. Competition (tanafus) is like rivalry over a thing and contending for it.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And its mixture is from Tasnim﴾. Concerning it there are two opinions:

(p-60) One: it is the name of a spring in Paradise which the closest ones drink pure, and which is mixed for the people of the right hand.

The second: Tasnim is water. This was said by al-Dahhak. Muqatil said: it is called Tasnim because it rises over (yatasannamu ‘alayhi) from the Garden of Eden, and it pours down upon them in a pouring, and they drink the wine from that water. Ibn Qutaybah said: it is said that Tasnim is the highest drink in Paradise. It is also said that it mixes with water descending from Tasnim, meaning from a height. Its root is from the hump of a camel, and from the raised top of graves. This is more pleasing to me, because of the words of al-Musayyib ibn ‘Alas describing a woman:

"As if her saliva, for the mixing, is from the snow of Tasnim, wine mixed with it."

He meant: as if her saliva were wine mixed with snow of Tasnim, meaning a mountain. Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is: and its mixture is from Tasnim, a spring that comes to them from Tasnim, meaning from a height that rises over them from the chambers. So "‘aynan" in this opinion is in the accusative, as He said: ﴿or feeding in a day of hunger, an orphan﴾ [Al-Balad: 15]. It is also permissible for "‘aynan" to be in the accusative by the phrase "they will be given to drink ‘aynan," meaning from a spring. We have already explained the meaning of "yashrabu biha" in [Hal Ata: 6].

(p-54) His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Nay!﴾ is a rebuke and a deterrence, meaning: the matter is not as they are upon, so let them desist. Here, according to many scholars, the speech is complete. Abu Hatim used to say: "Kallaa" is a beginning that connects with what follows, in the sense of "truly." ﴿Indeed, the record of the wicked﴾. Muqatil said: indeed the record of their deeds ﴿is in Sijjin﴾. Concerning Sijjin there are four opinions.

The first: it is the seventh earth. This is the view of Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, Ibn Zayd and Muqatil. It is narrated from Mujahid that he said: "Sijjin" is a rock beneath the seventh earth, and the record of the wicked is placed beneath it. This is a sign of their loss and an indication of the lowliness of their station.

The second: the meaning is that their record is in a low state (safal), as said by al-Hasan.

The third: it is ﴿in loss﴾, as said by Ikrimah.

The fourth: it is ﴿in confinement﴾, a form (fi‘}il) derived from "prison (sijn)," as said by Abu ‘Ubaydah.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And what will make you know what Sijjin is?﴾ This is an exaltation of its matter. Al-Zajjaj said: meaning, this is not something you or your people knew.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿It is a written record﴾, meaning: that book which is in Sijjin is a written record (p-55), i.e., inscribed. Ibn Qutaybah said: "al-raqm" means writing. Abu Dhu'ayb said:

"I recognized the abodes like the inscription of an ink-pot, which the Himyarite scribe writes out."

Al-Zajjaj recited it as "yadhburuha" with a dhal and a kasra on the ba'. Al-Asma‘i said: it is said "zabara" meaning he wrote, and "dhabara" meaning he read. Abu ‘Amr narrated from Tha‘lab, from Ibn al-A‘rabi, who said: the correct form is "zabartu" with a zay, meaning I wrote; and "dhabartu" with a dhal, meaning I perfected what I memorised. He said: the verse is "yazburuha," with a zay and a damma. Ibn Qutaybah said: it is narrated as "yazburuha" and "yadhburuha," and both are the same. It is said: zabara al-kitab yazburuhu and yazbiruhu, and dhabarahu yadhburuhu and yadhbiruhu. Qatadah said: "ruqqima lahu bi-sharr," as if he was marked with a sign by which it is known that he is a disbeliever. It has also been said that the meaning is: it is fixed for them like a mark on cloth, which is neither forgotten nor erased until they are recompensed for it.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Woe on that day to the deniers﴾. This is connected to His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿the day when mankind stands﴾, and what lies between them is an interjected speech. What follows has already been explained up to His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Rather, what they have earned has rusted over their hearts﴾. Ibn Kathir, Abu ‘Amr and Ibn ‘Amir read "bal ran" with a fatha on the ra' and with idgham (assimilation). Abu Bakr, on the authority of ‘Asim, read "bal rran" with idgham and a kasra on the ra'. Hafs, on the authority of ‘Asim, read "bal" with the lam clearly pronounced and "ran" with a fatha on the ra'. The linguists said: meaning it overcame their hearts. It is said: intoxicant wine "tarin" upon the intellect of the drunkard. Al-Zajjaj said: it was read with idgham of the lam into the ra' because of the closeness of the two letters, and clear pronunciation of the lam is permissible, because "bal" is one word and "ran" is another word. It is said: sin "raana" upon his heart, "yareenu raynan," when his heart is covered over (p-56). It is also said: "ghana yaghinu ghaynan," and the ghayn is like a thin cloud, while the rayn is like rust that covers the heart. I heard our shaykh Abu Mansur the linguist say: the word "ghayn" is used with the ra' and with the ghayn; the Qur'an has "Kallaa bal raana," and in a hadith: "Indeed it is veiled over my heart (layughanu ‘ala qalbi)." Likewise "al-rayah" (banner) is said with the ra' and with the ghayn, and "al-Rumaysa'" is written with the ghayn and with the ra', because "al-ramas" is written with both. The exegetes said: when their disobediences and sins multiplied, they encompassed their hearts. Al-Hasan said: it is sin upon sin until the heart becomes blind.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Nay!﴾, meaning: they do not believe. Then He began anew: ﴿Indeed, from their Lord, on that day, they will be veiled﴾. Ibn ‘Abbas said: indeed they will be veiled from seeing their Lord on that day, whereas the believer is not veiled from seeing Him. Malik ibn Anas said: when He veiled His enemies so that they did not see Him, He manifested Himself to His friends until they saw Him. Al-Shafi‘i said: when He veiled a people through wrath, this indicates that another people will see Him through good pleasure. Al-Zajjaj said: in this verse there is evidence that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will be seen (p-57) on the Day of Resurrection. Were it not so, there would be no benefit in this verse, nor would the disbelievers' station be debased by their being veiled from their Lord. Then after their being veiled from Allah, they enter the Fire, and that is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Then indeed they are the ones who will burn in Hell﴾.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Then it will be said﴾, meaning: the keepers of the Fire will say to them: ﴿This is the punishment which you used to deny.﴾ ﴿Nay!﴾, meaning: he does not believe in the punishment in which he burns. Then He informed where the place of ﴿the record of the righteous﴾ is, and He said, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, it is in ‘Illiyyin﴾. Concerning it there are seven opinions.

The first: it is Paradise. This was narrated by ‘Ata' from Ibn ‘Abbas.

The second: it is a tablet of green emerald, suspended beneath the Throne, in which their deeds are written. This is also narrated from Ibn ‘Abbas.

The third: it is the seventh heaven, and in it are the spirits of the believers. This was said by Ka‘b, and it is the view of Mujahid and Ibn Zayd.

The fourth: it is the right pillar of the Throne. This was said by Qatadah. Muqatil said: it is the leg (saq) of the Throne.

The fifth: it is the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary (Sidrat al-Muntaha). This was said by al-Dahhak.

The sixth: it is in height and ascent toward Allah, Mighty and Majestic. This was said by al-Hasan. Al-Farra’ said: in elevation upon elevation.

The seventh: it is the highest of places. This was said by al-Zajjaj.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And what will make you know what ‘Illiyyun is?﴾ This is an exaltation of its status.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿It is a written record﴾. The discussion concerning it is like the discussion concerning the verse before it.

(p-58) His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Witnessed by those brought near﴾, meaning: the angels brought near attend that written record, or that book when it is raised to ‘Illiyyun. What follows this has already been explained [Al-Infitar: 13], up to His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿looking﴾. Concerning it there are two opinions:

One: at what Allah has given them of honour.

The second: at their enemies when they are being punished.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿You will recognize in their faces the radiance of bliss﴾. Abu Ja‘far and Ya‘qub read "tu‘raf" with a damma on the ta' and a fatha on the ra', and "nadrah" in the nominative. Al-Farra’ said: the sheen of bliss and its moisture. The exegetes said: when you see them, you know that they are from the people of bliss, because of the beauty and light you see. Concerning "al-Raheeq" there are three opinions.

One: it is wine. This is the view of the majority. Then they differed as to which wine it is, with four opinions. One: the finest wine, said by al-Khalil ibn Ahmad. The second: wine purified from adulteration, said by al-Akhfash. The third: white wine, said by Muqatil. The fourth: aged wine, related by Ibn Qutaybah.

The second opinion: it is a spring in Paradise mixed with musk, said by al-Hasan.

The third: it is the drink that has no adulteration in it, said by Ibn Qutaybah and al-Zajjaj. Concerning His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿sealed﴾ there are three opinions:

One: mixed, said by Ibn Mas‘ud.

The second: sealed on its vessel. Mujahid went in this direction.

(p-59) The third: it has a seal, i.e., the outcome of a scent, and that outcome is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Its seal is musk﴾, meaning its outcome. This is the view of Abu ‘Ubaydah.

His saying: ﴿Its seal is musk﴾. Ibn Kathir, ‘Asim, Nafi‘, Abu ‘Amr, Ibn ‘Amir and Hamzah read "khitamuhu" with a kasra on the kha', a fatha on the ta', and an alif after them both, with the mim in the nominative. Al-Kisa’i read "khatamuhu" with a fatha on the kha', an alif after it, and then a fatha on the ta'. Al-Shaizari narrated "khatimuhu" in the same way, except that he reads the ta' with a kasra. Ubayy ibn Ka‘b, ‘Urwah and Abu al-‘Aliyah read "khatamuhu" with a fatha on the kha' and the ta', and a damma on the mim, without an alif.

Concerning His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Its seal is musk﴾, the exegetes have four opinions:

One: its mixture is musk, said by Ibn Mas‘ud and Mujahid.

The second: its sealing, with which the vessel is sealed, is musk, [said by Ibn ‘Abbas].

The third: its taste and its fragrance are musk, said by ‘Alqamah.

The fourth: the last of its taste is musk, [said by] Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, al-Farra’, Abu ‘Ubaydah, Ibn Qutaybah, al-Zajjaj and others.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And for that let the competitors compete﴾, meaning: let them strive to obtain it, and let them be eager for it through obedience to Allah. Competition (tanafus) is like rivalry over a thing and contending for it.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And its mixture is from Tasnim﴾. Concerning it there are two opinions:

(p-60) One: it is the name of a spring in Paradise which the closest ones drink pure, and which is mixed for the people of the right hand.

The second: Tasnim is water. This was said by al-Dahhak. Muqatil said: it is called Tasnim because it rises over (yatasannamu ‘alayhi) from the Garden of Eden, and it pours down upon them in a pouring, and they drink the wine from that water. Ibn Qutaybah said: it is said that Tasnim is the highest drink in Paradise. It is also said that it mixes with water descending from Tasnim, meaning from a height. Its root is from the hump of a camel, and from the raised top of graves. This is more pleasing to me, because of the words of al-Musayyib ibn ‘Alas describing a woman:

"As if her saliva, for the mixing, is from the snow of Tasnim, wine mixed with it."

He meant: as if her saliva were wine mixed with snow of Tasnim, meaning a mountain. Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is: and its mixture is from Tasnim, a spring that comes to them from Tasnim, meaning from a height that rises over them from the chambers. So "‘aynan" in this opinion is in the accusative, as He said: ﴿or feeding in a day of hunger, an orphan﴾ [Al-Balad: 15]. It is also permissible for "‘aynan" to be in the accusative by the phrase "they will be given to drink ‘aynan," meaning from a spring. We have already explained the meaning of "yashrabu biha" in [Hal Ata: 6].

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 83, verse 29–36:

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, those who committed crimes﴾, that is, those who associated partners with Allah, ﴿used to laugh at those who believed﴾, meaning the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), such as ʿAmmar, Bilal, Khabbab, and others, ﴿laughing﴾ in mockery of them. ﴿And when they passed by them﴾, meaning the believers, ﴿by them﴾, that is, by the disbelievers, ﴿they winked at one another﴾, that is, they signaled with the eyelid and the eyebrow in mockery of them. ﴿And when they returned to their own people﴾, meaning the disbelievers, ﴿they returned jesting﴾, that is, marveling at what they were in, taking delight in mentioning them. Abu Jaʿfar, Hafs on the authority of ʿAsim, and ʿAbd al-Razzaq on the authority of Ibn ʿAmir recited: "fakihin" without an alif. We have explained the meaning of the two recitations under [Ya-Sin: 55]. ﴿And when they saw them﴾, that is, they saw the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), ﴿they said: Indeed, these are surely astray.﴾ Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Yet they had not been sent as guardians over them﴾, meaning the disbelievers were not sent as guardians over the believers, ﴿guarding their deeds over them﴾, that is, they had not been entrusted with guarding their deeds. ﴿So today﴾, meaning in the Hereafter, ﴿those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers﴾ when they see them being punished in the Fire. Abu Salih said: It is said to the people of the Fire while they are in it: "Go out," and its gates are opened for them; but when they approach, wishing to leave, its gates are closed in front of them. As for the believers, ﴿they will be on couches, looking on﴾ at the punishment of their enemy. Muqatil said: For every man of the people of Paradise there is a window through which he looks at the enemies of Allah and how they are punished, and so they praise Allah for what He has honored them with. They converse with the people of the Fire and the people of the Fire converse with them, until the Fire closes over its inhabitants, and then the openings are sealed.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Have the disbelievers been rewarded?﴾ Hamza, al-Kisai, and Harun on the authority of Abu ʿAmr recited: ﴿hal thuwwiba﴾ with the lam assimilated. That is: have they been repaid and recompensed for their mockery of the believers in the world? This interrogative is in the sense of affirmation (taqrir).
